title: Don't scan random QR codes
revealText1: These are technical details your browser automatically sent just because you scanned a QR code.
revealText2: A QR code is not just an image. It is a gateway that can lead anywhere — and every website you open learns at least this:
whyTitle: Why scanning random QR codes is risky
whyList: A QR code can lead to phishing or a malicious website.
It can trigger a download of harmful files.
It can trick you into logging into a fake service.
It can be placed over a legitimate QR code.
You cannot know where it leads until it's too late.
geoNote: Geolocation and internet provider are determined from IP address via Cloudflare – accuracy at country level.
nocookiesText1: No cookies, no trackers, no third-party analytics. Everything stays in your browser.
nocookiesText2: The goal is to show how easily any website can collect technical information about your device — without consent.
motivationText: People scan QR codes without thinking. This project is a simple demonstration of what you reveal by doing so.
contactText: If you want to extend this project or build your own awareness campaign:
trainingText: We recommend BOIT Cyber Security.

bannerDesktop.title: Looks like you're on a computer
bannerDesktop.text: QR codes are mostly scanned on mobile — that's fine. Statistics count desktop and mobile separately, so this visit will show up under Desktop. If you still care about what you reveal, read on — it applies to every device.

bannerBot.title: Automated access detected
bannerBot.text: It looks like this page is being visited by a bot or automated tool. This visit will not be counted in statistics, but is logged for audit purposes.

bannerReturning.title: We recognised you
bannerReturning.text:
You've visited this page once already today. We recognised you by your device fingerprint — no cookies, no login, no interaction required.
This is exactly what any website can do.
